id.description: Stable slug; kebab-case; unique across all meshes

category.description: One of: proxy, search, ocr, geo, nlp, content, domains, security, recon, infrastructure, web_analysis, visualization, registry, dashboard

kind.description: What kind of deployable this is. Orthogonal to mesh. 'container' = runs as a Docker service on the dockerhost (has host_port, container_port, /health, Dockerfile, deploy.yaml, LXC workspace). 'static' = static GitHub Pages site (no port, no container, no workspace, no /health). fleet-runner gates kind-specific operations on this field — kind=static is skipped by health/smoke/deploy/clone-missing/audit-port/bump-version/update-dep.

language.description: Primary implementation language. For kind=container this drives bulk-operation filters (e.g. 'update-dep' only touches go services). For kind=static it is informational. Default for legacy 0exec/0crawl entries is 'go'; default for pages is 'html'.

runtime.description: How the service is started/managed. Orthogonal to kind and language — gates deploy logic (compose: `docker compose up -d`; systemd: `systemctl restart`; github-pages: trigger Pages rebuild). Default for kind=container is 'compose'; default for kind=static is 'github-pages'. Adding a new runtime is how the fleet absorbs deployment shapes without forking every audit.

url.description: Public base URL of the service, no trailing slash

example_path.description: Path + query that produces a real response; begins with '/'. Example: '/?url=https://example.com'. May be empty if the service has no canonical example.

path_template.description: auth=path_token: how the token is embedded in the path, with '{token}' placeholder. Example: '/t/{token}'

public_demo_token.description: auth=path_token: an intentionally-public demo token consumers may default to. NEVER include real secrets here.

auth_help.description: Canonical short label for what auth a caller needs. Computed by generate.py from the auth object. UIs render verbatim — do NOT re-derive in JS/templates (that's what produced the historical 'No auth' bug on api_key services).

pages_url.description: kind=static only. Canonical GitHub Pages URL. For kind=container this field MUST NOT be set.

pages_source_branch.description: kind=static only. Branch the Pages build is served from (typically 'main' or 'gh-pages'). Informational for the catalog UI.

port.description: DEPRECATED — ambiguous (host vs container). Use host_port / container_port instead.

host_port.description: Port bound on the dockerhost. This is what the gateway nginx proxy_pass points at. Single source of truth for IaC rendering. See private fleet-state/OPS.md for the dockerhost address.

container_port.description: Port the service listens on INSIDE the container. Informational; not used by gateway routing.

trl.description: Technology Readiness Level achieved. 1-3 toy, 4-5 developing, 6-7 real, 8-9 production. Optional; absence means not yet assessed.

trl_evidence.description: One-line justification for the TRL number (what concretely makes it that level).

trl_ceiling.description: Maximum TRL realistically achievable with CPU-only smart logic + free public data. Null means no known ceiling. Repos with low ceilings are deprecation candidates.

trl_ceiling_reason.description: One-line reason for the ceiling (e.g. 'needs libpostal trained data', 'requires DOM canary injection', 'wraps paid threat intel feeds').

trl_assessed_at.description: ISO date the TRL was last evaluated. Re-assess if older than ~90 days.

trl_assessor.description: Who/what assessed: 'claude-session-YYYY-MM-DD' for AI-assisted, 'human' for manual review.

placement.description: Whether this service is a safe dynamic-placement candidate. See ADR-0039. 'pinned' = holds state that doesn't trivially move with it (a data volume, a database, anything where starting it elsewhere loses or orphans data) — never route dynamically as-is. 'replicable' = safe to start on any capacity-eligible host. Optional, same convention as `trl`: absence means not yet assessed, NOT a default of either value — do not assume unset means replicable just because most kind=container entries are. Declared per-slug in overrides.json.

depends_on.description: Declared service-to-service dependencies (slugs). Static counterpart to the live edges in go-fleet-graph. fleet-runner audit-graph diffs declared vs observed: declared-not-observed = dead dep (remove) or broken caller; observed-not-declared = undeclared coupling (add or refactor). Optional; absence means 'no declared deps yet'. Edges to non-fleet hosts go in tags, not here.

owner.description: Who is responsible for this service. F4 phase 1 — OPTIONAL while the fleet backfills organically; track compliance via 'fleet-runner audit service-yaml-schema --field owner'. INTERNAL ONLY: not exposed in services-public.json (not added to PUBLIC_FIELDS).

contact.description: Canonical contact — email, slack handle, mailing list.

github.description: Optional GitHub login used as default assignee for issues / PRs auto-filed against this service.

mcp_ready.description: True if this service serves a live GET /agent.json and is currently aggregated into go-fleet-mcp-gateway's MCP tool list. Set by bin/audit_mcp_ready.py from the gateway's own GET /gateway/tools — never hand-set. Absence means not yet assessed or not currently reachable; false is not written, only true (see services.mcp.json).

mcp_tool_count.description: How many MCP tools this service currently contributes to the gateway's aggregation. Companion to mcp_ready.

mcp_assessed_at.description: Timestamp of the audit_mcp_ready.py run that last confirmed mcp_ready.

network_exposure.description: How reachable this service actually is, computed by bin/generate.py from cert_domain/auth.type/scope (see compute_network_exposure) — not hand-declared for entries with a rendered vhost, so it can't drift from what nginx-render actually emits. 'loopback' = 127.0.0.1-only, unreachable even fleet-wide. 'lan-internal' = host-network/0.0.0.0-bound, reachable over the private LAN but never proxied through nginx (no vhost, no public DNS) — set via a manual overrides.json override since the registry alone can't distinguish this from loopback. 'gateway-ip-allowlisted' = public vhost + DNS, gated only by an nginx IP allowlist (successor to the old `scope: internal-only` flag). 'gateway-authenticated' = public vhost + DNS, keystore auth_request-gated (the common case). 'gateway-public' = public vhost + DNS, auth.type=none, genuinely open. Absent for kind=static (not a listening service). Excluded from services-public.json — see PUBLIC_FIELDS in bin/generate.py.
